wu: Toy Charades: Teacher acts out a toy (e.g., bouncing a ball), students guess 'Is it a ball?', teacher replies 'Yes, it is!' or 'No, it isn't!'.
wuAlt: Toy Flashcard Race: Two teams race to match toy flashcards to pictures on the board.
Toy Sound Game: Teacher makes toy sounds (car vroom, doll giggle), students name the toy.
pres: Show toy flashcards (ball, doll, car, teddy, puzzle) with adjectives (big, small, red, blue, green). Model sentences: 'It is a big red car.' Students repeat chorally. Ask 'What is it?' and elicit full sentences.
presAlt: Toy Storybook: Read a simple story like 'The Big Red Ball', highlighting adjectives. Point to toys and ask 'What is it?'
Realia Show: Bring real toys to class, describe them, pass them around for students to feel and describe.
prac: Guessing Game: Teams take turns. One student describes a toy (e.g., 'It is a small blue doll.'), team guesses 'Is it a doll?'. Teacher monitors for correct word order and adjectives.
pracAlt: Toy Description Relay: Teams line up, first student runs to flashcards, picks one, describes it, next student continues.
Adjective Match: Students match toy flashcards to adjective cards (e.g., 'car' + 'red' = 'red car').
ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher says 'Draw a big green teddy', students draw. Check drawings to confirm comprehension of two-adjective descriptions.
re: Toy TPR: Teacher shouts 'Be a big car!' students move arms like wheels, 'Be a small doll!' students tiptoe and giggle.
prod: Toy Shop Roleplay: One student is shopkeeper, others are customers. Customers say 'Can I have the small blue puzzle, please?', shopkeeper hands it over. Swap roles.
rw: Trace and Copy: Students trace toy words (ball, doll, car, teddy, puzzle) and copy them twice. Then write sentences: 'I have got a big red ball.'
st: Read 'The Toy Box' story with repeated toy descriptions. Sing 'The Teddy Bear Song' (to the tune of 'Twinkle Twinkle'). Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teacher removes a toy from a line, students say 'The big red ball is missing!'
Students sit in a circle, each adds a toy with an adjective: 'I have a big ball, a small doll...'
Students mark toy flashcards as teacher calls them out with adjectives
Students sort toy flashcards into 'big' and 'small' piles
First student asks 'Do you have a doll?', next answers and asks another student
diff: Fast finishers: Draw their own toy and write three sentences about it.
Support: Use word banks with toy names and adjectives for writing tasks.
hw: Write the toys words twice in your notebook, once in rainbow colours.
Draw your favourite toy and write one sentence: 'It is a ____ ____ ____.'
Ask your family: 'What is your favourite toy?' and tell the class next week.
tip: Use local Moroccan toys like 'taqcha nqaqa' (wooden tops) to connect the theme to students' lives, making vocabulary more meaningful and culturally relevant.
